findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define the exact commit set the DET check compares: only COMMITS-event-linked shas, or also trailer-referencing commits discovered via git log — name the discovery mechanism.
evidence: "when a ticket records file_impact AND linked/referencing commits are found"
'referencing' has no defined provenance vs 'linked' (COMMITS event)
findings.finding: Step 3 introduces 'linked/referencing commits are found' but never states how 'referencing' commits are discovered (git log scan for rebar-ticket trailers? only COMMITS-event linked shas?). The data source for the diff comparison is unspecified.
scenarios: Executor must guess whether to git-log-scan for trailers or use only attach_commits/COMMITS-linked shas, producing different check populations
findings.suggested_fix: State: 'the commit set = shas from COMMITS events attached to the ticket (union), no git-log trailer scan.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile step 3's 'tests/docs conventions per existing gate rules' with the codebase: the only extant path exemption (orchestrator.bug_blast_radius_escalates) covers tests/ + conftest.py, NOT docs/ — either name the docs allowance as new behavior the plan introduces (and specify its predicate) or drop 'docs' and reuse the existing tests-only classifier.
evidence: Plan step 3: 'allowing tests/docs conventions per existing gate rules'
AC #3 does not restate the allowance but step 3 is its basis
src/rebar/llm/plan_review/orchestrator.py:208 — the sole extant path classifier: `if p.startswith("tests/") or p.rsplit("/", 1)[-1] == "conftest.py": continue` (tests only, no docs)
search for `startswith("docs` returned no matches; no docs/ exemption exists in any gate
findings.finding: Step 3 and AC #3 justify the DET close check's docs allowance by 'existing gate rules', but the only extant path-exemption convention (bug_blast_radius_escalates) exempts tests/ and conftest.py only — no gate rule anywhere exempts docs/ paths, so the cited reusable rule for docs does not exist.
scenarios: A commit linked via attach-commits touches a docs/ file outside declared file_impact; the plan implies an existing rule permits this, but the implementer finds no such rule and must invent a docs convention (new behavior, out of scope) or block conforming docs-only changes.
findings.suggested_fix: Either (a) reuse the existing tests-only predicate (tests/ + conftest.py) and remove the 'docs' claim, or (b) explicitly declare a new docs/ exemption as in-scope new behavior in step 3, defining the exact path predicate rather than attributing it to a preexisting rule.

findings.checklist_item: Specify in step 3 exactly which commit set drives the changed-path union (state.commits from attach_commits, the trailer-referencing scan, or their union) and how it relates to the existing _referencing_commit_exists descendant-crediting logic.
evidence: Plan: 'when a ticket records file_impact AND linked/referencing commits are found, compare the union of those commits' changed paths'
close_precheck._referencing_commit_exists (close_precheck.py:94) scans git log for rebar-ticket: trailers / '<id>:' subjects and accepts a commit for the ticket OR any transitive descendant

attach_commits (src/rebar/_lib_writes.py:697) records SHAs into state.commits via a COMMITS event; these need carry no trailer, so a repaired ticket's state.commits and the trailer-scan set can diverge
findings.finding: Step 3 conflates two distinct commit sets — attach_commits-populated state.commits vs. the trailer-based referencing-commit scan — without saying which one supplies the 'changed paths' union for the comparison.
scenarios: An agent botches the trailer, then repairs via `rebar attach-commits`; state.commits now holds the SHA but the trailer scan still misses it — does the new check run off state.commits, the scan, or the union?
A descendant's referencing commit satisfies the existing gate but is not in the closing ticket's state.commits
findings.suggested_fix: State that the check unions changed paths from the ticket's recorded state.commits (the attach-commits target) so the repair verb directly feeds it, and note whether descendant commits are included as they are in the existing referencing-commit gate.

findings.checklist_item: Name the concrete exemption primitive step 3 reuses (e.g. is_test_material for tests/conftest) and define explicitly whether/how docs paths are exempted, since no existing close-gate rule classifies changed diff paths.
evidence: Plan: 'a changed path outside the declared impact (allowing tests/docs conventions per existing gate rules)'
No close_precheck rule classifies changed diff paths today (searched _commands; only _referencing_commit_exists exists)

orchestrator.bug_blast_radius_escalates (orchestrator.py:191) classifies DECLARED file_impact test paths; bugfix_size_gate.is_test_material (bugfix_size_gate.py:92) classifies code-review diff paths — neither is a close-time changed-path exemption
findings.finding: Step 3's 'allowing tests/docs conventions per existing gate rules' points to close-surface gate rules that do not exist; the only comparable path classifiers operate on declared file_impact or code-review diffs, so the exemption primitive is unspecified.
scenarios: Implementer looks for an 'existing gate rule' that exempts tests/docs at close and finds none, then hand-rolls a divergent classifier
A docs-only or tests-only commit path trips the new BLOCK because 'docs' is named but no existing rule actually exempts docs (the test-material classifiers cover tests/conftest, not docs)
findings.suggested_fix: Reuse rebar.llm.code_review.bugfix_size_gate.is_test_material (tests/** + conftest.py) for the test exemption and spell out the docs-path rule explicitly rather than deferring to unnamed 'existing gate rules'.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Place the 'SHA resolves in the repo' validation in the shared `attach_commits` engine seam (the `*_core`/reducer write path) so the CLI, MCP tool, and library facade all inherit rejection of unresolvable SHAs, rather than validating only in the CLI verb.
evidence: Step 1 attaches SHA validation to the CLI verb: 'validate each SHA resolves in the repo'

Step 2 describes the MCP tool and library re-export as routing through the same seam but does not state that SHA validation lives in the seam: 'Library re-export ... and MCP tool (`attach_commits`) with outputSchema'
AC line 1 tests invalid-SHA rejection via `tests/unit -k attach_commits` but does not pin the rejection to the shared core
findings.finding: SHA validation ('validate each SHA resolves in the repo') is placed in the CLI verb wrapper (step 1) rather than in the shared `attach_commits` engine seam, so the MCP `attach_commits` tool and the `rebar.attach_commits` library facade can record a COMMITS event with an unresolvable SHA.
findings.location: Plan step 1: 'CLI verb `rebar attach-commits <ticket> <sha>...` wrapping the existing `rebar.attach_commits` seam (validate each SHA resolves in the repo; union-add semantics unchanged).'
scenarios: MCP client issues `attach_commits` with a bogus SHA — if validation is CLI-only, the tool records an invalid COMMITS event with no rejection
Library caller invokes `rebar.attach_commits(ticket, ['deadbeef'])` directly and bypasses the CLI's resolve check, persisting an unresolvable reference
findings.suggested_fix: State in step 1/2 that SHA-resolution validation lives in `attach_commits` core (the shared seam), with the CLI/MCP/library layers doing only parsing and error formatting on top; keep AC line 1's test exercising the seam directly.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Acknowledge that the new close-gate BLOCK changes close behavior for existing tickets with file_impact+linked commits, and state the remedy (fix file_impact, or an explicit override) — not just the happy conforming case.
evidence: "a changed path outside the declared impact ... is a deterministic close BLOCK"
COMMITS event 'already exist (used by the code-review workflow)' per Context — existing tickets carry linked commits
findings.finding: The new DET close-gate BLOCK changes existing close behavior: tickets that already have file_impact and linked commits (e.g. via the code-review COMMITS flow) could newly fail to close once this gate lands. The plan does not acknowledge this as a behavior change or give a false-positive escape/override.
scenarios: An in-flight ticket with legitimately broader commits than its file_impact suddenly cannot close after this gate ships

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify partial-failure semantics for multi-SHA attach (reject the whole batch atomically vs attach-valid-and-report-invalid) and cover it in a unit test.
evidence: "validate each SHA resolves in the repo"
AC1: 'invalid SHAs are rejected with a clear error' — singular framing, silent on mixed batches
findings.finding: The multi-SHA verb has no stated atomicity/partial-failure semantics: `attach-commits <ticket> <sha>...` validates 'each SHA resolves', but if some resolve and some do not, the plan does not say whether it rejects all (atomic) or attaches the valid ones and reports the rest.
scenarios: User passes 5 shas, one typo'd; unclear if the other 4 get attached or the whole call fails
findings.suggested_fix: Adopt fail-atomic: validate all shas first; if any fails, reject the whole call and record no event.

findings.checklist_item: Reconcile step 3's hard-BLOCK disposition with the advisory treatment of off-file_impact DET matches (test_det_invariants.py:270); justify why an off-scope changed path is blocking here or downgrade it to advisory to avoid false-positive close blocks on legitimate scope expansion.
evidence: Plan: 'a changed path outside the declared impact ... is a deterministic close BLOCK'
tests/unit/test_det_invariants.py:270 test_project_det_match_off_file_impact_is_advisory asserts a match on a path NOT in file_impact yields status=fail with blocking=False (advisory, not blocking)
Plan's own scope note concedes 'linked commits may be incomplete even when they match file_impact' — i.e. the linkage/impact relationship is loose
findings.finding: Making an off-scope changed path a hard deterministic BLOCK conflicts with the established codebase precedent that off-file_impact DET matches are advisory, and risks false-positive blocks on legitimate scope expansion.
scenarios: Author legitimately expands the change (touches a helper not pre-declared in file_impact) and gets hard-blocked at close despite doing the work correctly
file_impact was recorded early and the implementation reasonably grew — the BLOCK penalizes accurate-but-broader work

evidence: 2 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).

verify command `grep assertions in the docs test tier.` greps the unanchored word 'assertions' — it substring-matches (e.g. 'review_assertions'); anchor it (\b, ^$, or a quoted key like '"assertions":')
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.finding: Step 3's DET check should explicitly reuse the existing referencing-commit discovery and file_impact close-gate machinery rather than build parallel logic. The codebase already has _referencing_commit_exists (close_precheck.py:94) and referencing_commit_diffs (completion_prefetch.py:284) for discovering commits by rebar-ticket trailer/subject, an existing file_impact-driven DET close gate (close_precheck.py:267-277), and test-path classification in bug_blast_radius_escalates (orchestrator.py:191-211). The plan names 'linked/referencing commits' discovery, a close BLOCK, and 'tests/docs conventions' classification without naming these existing seams as the reuse basis.
scenarios: Author writes fresh git-log/diff parsing and a new test-path classifier instead of extending the existing helpers, duplicating trailer-resolution and path-normalization logic
